_doc: Ledger of cartoon shorts (the daily automatic method). The producer appends one entry with status 'produced'; the publish job turns it into 'published'. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a topic listed here.

episodes.title: What If You Jumped Into a Hole Through the Earth?
episodes.topic: falling through a tunnel through the centre of the Earth (gravity tunnel, 38 minutes one way, oscillates forever)

episodes.title: What If You Had to Eat Like a Hummingbird? 🍔
episodes.topic: a man with a hummingbird's energy use per gram: 120,000 calories a day, a burger every three minutes, and too little skin to lose 6 kW of heat (square-cube law); the bird's own answer is nightly torpor
episodes.trend: youtube_shorts: the week's top 'what if' row is 'What If Humans Had Hummingbird Hearts' (3.95M views/day) plus an Arabic remake; body and everyday scenarios beat space topics
episodes.note: uploaded private from the rehearsal session, published by the owner; retitled 2026-11-15 from "What If You Had a Hummingbird's Metabolism? 🤔" (plain title test)

episodes.title: What If You Tried to Open a Plane Door Mid-Flight? ✈️
episodes.topic: trying to open an airliner's exit door at cruise: cabin pressure holds the plug door shut with almost 20,000 pounds (8 psi on 2,448 square inches, four cars); suction-cup analogy; it only lets go on the ground
episodes.trend: youtube_shorts: 'What if a Plane Door Opened Mid-flight' (2.11M views/day) is the strongest undone 'what if' row; everyday travel scenarios win for several channels this week

episodes.title: What If You Ran in Cinderella's Glass Slippers? 👠
episodes.topic: running in glass slippers: squeezed glass holds about 1000 MPa (a 1 cm cube carries ten tons, two elephants), stretched glass about 40 MPa, twenty-five times less, because of microscopic surface scratches; a running step bends the heel and it snaps; bag-of-chips notch analogy
episodes.trend: youtube_shorts: the Cinderella's-slipper question wins for three channels this week (lilBrain 1.76M views/day, Den TV 0.81M, HawdAlafkar 0.61M); we take the theme and ask the physical question

episodes.title: What If the Elevator Cable Snapped? 😱
episodes.topic: every rope of an elevator snaps at once: each of the six ropes could carry the loaded car alone (factor of safety 10.25), and if all part, the overspeed governor trips wedge brakes on the guide rails; the car falls about five feet (3.4 to 7.3 ft) in about a second; a last-second jump takes off at 6 mph against 76 mph; seat-belt analogy; the brakes only release when the car is lifted
episodes.trend: topic_bank: elevator-cable-snaps (44 elevator shorts, 60M views, 43 channels; 'cable snaps' videos reach 27k to 178k views on channels with 50 to 1,250 subscribers); today's trend file has no fresh everyday row that is not already made
